newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India-Kuwait start term oil product contract talks.
newsitem.headline: India-Kuwait start term oil product contract talks.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has started talks this week with Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC) to renew its annual oil products term purchase contracts which have been delayed since May, industry sources said on Tuesday.
They said the talks had been delayed due to Indian general elections in May and the subsequent changes in Government.

The IOC team has been in Kuwait since Monday to discuss and set the terms for IOC's purchases of high speed diesel and superior kerosene for the last five months and for the next seven months, they said.

The two parties are to discuss price terms, volumes as well as product grade, as in the case of diesel. The diesel grade will be a factor this time because India now seeks more 0.5 percent sulphur diesel, while its previous contracts involve the 1.0-percent grade.
However, it is not likely that India would take any 0.25 percent sulphur diesel under this term contract as its total requirements are currently not very large.

IOC on Tuesday cancelled its tender to buy diesel for November delivery, after buying a mere 120,000 tonnes for October and 255,000 tonnes for September. This is a far cry from the 7.4 million tonnes it bought between January and August.
IOC imported about 900,000 tonnes of diesel and 1.08 million tonnes of kerosene from KPC in its 1995-1996 term deal.
The sources said IOC would first seal its contract with KPC and then use the terms as a benchmark for its talks with Bahrain National Oil Co (BANOCO) and Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC).

IOC has been buying the 0.25 percent sulphur grade through monthly spot tenders since end-July and has since been importing about 60,000-90,000 tonnes a month. This is to prepare the country for a gradual switch from the higher sulphur grade by April 1999 to curb air pollution.
The sources said India would be expected to raise its volumes of diesel purchased through term contracts as they are seeking to buy less by monthly spot tenders.
Port congestions are also contributing to IOC's inability to buy too much monthly spot cargoes.
BANOCO supplied some 1.32 million tonnes of diesel and 720,000 tonnes kerosene while ADNOC supplied 500,000 tonne of diesel and 300,000 tonnes of kerosene in their 1995-1996 term contracts.
In fiscal 1995/1996, India imported 17 million tonnes of middle-distillates, out of which about 4.34 million tonnes were imported by term contracts with the three Gulf oil companies.
Last May, IOC bought through term tenders, two cargoes of kerosene and three cargoes of 0.5 percent sulphur diesel a month for deliveries between July 1996 and June 1997.

KPC was one of the winners in that tender, with its diesel price of $1.90 per barrel over MidEast quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to the Indian east coast. KPC sold kerosene a 39 cent premium to MidEast quotes on a free-on-board (fob) basis or $1.34 premium, c-and-f east coast. India's diesel demand is growing at an annual rate of 14.5 percent, government statistics state. Its demand is projected to grow from 35 million tonnes in 1996/1997, to 54 million tonnes by 2001/2002 and 77 million tonnes by 2006/2007.
